subject: Renewal + Mid-contract top-up: ForgeCare scaling and billing options
messages:
From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@forgecare.ai>
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@forgecare.ai>, Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@forgecare.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + top-up options (Q4 surge)

Hi David —

Thanks again for the demo last month. We expect a meaningful usage surge in Q4 due to a new pilot across two hospital systems. Before we finalize our renewal, procurement asked for: a) a short-term top-up to cover estimated Q4 overage (~40% above current committed units), b) an option to co-term to align renewal dates, and c) any possible tiered discount if we commit to a bigger annual cap.

High level asks:
- Immediate: temporary top-up of 40% capacity for Nov–Dec, invoiced pro-rata.
- Renewal: co-term existing contract to 2027-11-30 and evaluate a stepped uplift (10% discount band for +20% commit, 18% for +40%).
- Approval path: Procurement will need pricing and a simple SOW for approvals by 11/24.

Can you send options by EOD? We may need a quick PO.

Thanks —
Tom
Head of Platform, ForgeCare

--
Attachment: none referenced in this message

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@forgecare.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + top-up options (Q4 surge)

Tom —

Appreciate the heads up and congrats on the pilot ramp. We can support a short-term 40% top-up and present three paths for the renewal. Attached is a concise options sheet; summary below.

Quick summary (details in attached PDF):
1) Short-term bridge (Nov–Dec): one-off top-up invoice for 40% additional reserved units, pro-rated for 2 months. No long-term commitment.
2) Co-term + stepped uplift (recommended): convert top-up into a permanent uplift and co-term to 2027-11-30. Pricing tiers: +20% commit = 10% discount off list; +40% commit = 18% discount. Applied to committed units only.
3) Hybrid: 2-month top-up + option to annualize in Jan with credit for amounts already paid.

I included a sample SOW and the quote: ForgeCare-Updated-Quote-20261120.pdf. If procurement needs, we can expedite a DocuSign envelope.

Next steps: tell me which path you want and I’ll route for internal approval.

Best,
David Kim\Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + top-up options (internal: approval needed)

David — forwarding ForgeCare ask. Quick read: they want pricing + SOW by 11/24 and a mid-contract 40% top-up for Nov–Dec. Likely want to annualize.

My suggested concession framing:
- Approve the one-off top-up at list price but offer a 5% amortized credit if they annualize by Jan 31.
- For co-term uplift, we can stretch to 12% discount at +20% commit (instead of 10%) if they sign within 2 weeks — conditional on finance sign-off.

Irene/Jordan — do we have bandwidth to fast-track SOW and a short legal addendum? Any guardrails from finance on the 12%?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 12:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + top-up options (internal: approval needed)

Ben / David —

Finance comments: we can flex to 12% on the +20% band (one-time, time-bound) if we secure a firm annualized uplift and payment terms of Net30 with an upfront 30% deposit for the uplift portion. For +40% band the 18% stands but we need a minimum 60% upfront for the incremental portion or a 3-month amortization.

Legal: we should avoid re-doing the entire contract. SOW + amendment + co-term signature is fine — Jordan, please prepare a short amendment template.

Operational note: Engineering will need 48 hours notice for capacity pre-warming once the committed uplift is finalized. Include pre-warm SLA in the SOW.

I’ll approve routing this to Tom with the above guardrails.

Irene Choi\Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

> On Nov 20, 2026, at 11:05 AM, ben_carter@redwood.com wrote:
> David — forwarding ForgeCare ask. Quick read: they want pricing + SOW by 11/24 and a mid-contract 40% top-up for Nov–Dec. Likely want to annualize.

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@forgecare.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@forgecare.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + top-up options (Q4 surge)

Tom —

Thanks for the clarity. Per internal review, here are the firm options we can deliver by 11/24:

A) Short-term bridge (fast):
- 40% additional reserved units for Nov 1–Dec 31, invoiced pro-rata at list.
- No long-term commitment.
- Invoice estimate: $48,600 (pro-rata; details in attached PDF).

B) Co-term + stepped uplift (recommended for predictability):
- Co-term to 2027-11-30 and annualize uplift subject to committed bands:
  * +20% committed units = 12% discount (time-limited quote if signed by 12/4).
  * +40% committed units = 18% discount (requires 60% upfront or 3-month amortization).
- Payment terms: Net30 with 30% deposit on uplift at +20% band; higher deposit for +40%.
- Operational: 48-hour pre-warm window included in SOW.

C) Hybrid (short bridge → annualize):
- Pay short-term bridge now; if you annualize by Jan 31 we will credit 5% of the bridge amount against the first invoice of the annualized uplift.

Attachments: ForgeCare-Updated-Quote-20261120.pdf, SOW-ForgeCare-draft-20261120.docx

If procurement wants, we’ll create a DocuSign package and hold an internal 20-minute call to walk through the SOW and payment cadence. Please let me know which option you prefer and I’ll prepare the legal amendment and DocuSign.

Best,
David
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
